subject: Science
title: Small creatures
objectives: Children will look closely at small creatures with a magnifying glass.
Children will say that small creatures are looked at and not hurt.
content: Looking closely at ants, beetles, butterflies and bees, and learning to look without touching or hurting.
teachingActivities: Use magnifying glasses and a clear bug box with a lid; keep creatures only for a short time and return them; avoid stinging insects; always say "we look, we do not hurt"; wash hands after.
learnerActivities: Name small creatures, look at them carefully and be kind to them.
resources: A clear bug box with a lid
Pictures of an ant, a bee, a butterfly and a beetle
A garden or school yard area
assessment: Observe whether each child names two small creatures and looks gently without touching.
expectedOutcomes: Looks at a small creature gently without touching.
crossCurricular: Literacy: song about bees and ants

lessons.title: Ants and beetles
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name ants and beetles and look at them with a magnifying glass.
successCriteria: Names an ant and a beetle
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, their homes and babies and handle toys gently.
resources: Pictures of an ant and a beetle
A clear bug box with a lid
lessons.starter: Show the ant picture and say "This is an ant. It is very small. Let us look carefully."
teacherActivities: Show the pictures and say how many legs and what colour they are.
Show how to hold the magnifying glass and look closely.
Go outside and find a small creature in the garden with an adult.
Say "We look and we do not hurt" and wave goodbye to the creature.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children look at a picture through the glass.
Children look from a safe distance.
Children say "bye bye" and wave.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the pictures and say how many legs and what colour they are. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to hold the magnifying glass and look closely. Children: Children look at a picture through the glass.
Step 3. Teacher: Go outside and find a small creature in the garden with an adult. Children: Children look from a safe distance.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We look and we do not hurt" and wave goodbye to the creature. Children: Children say "bye bye" and wave.

practical.title: Look with a magnifier
steps: Give each child a turn to look through the glass.
Look at an ant or beetle without touching.
practical.safety: Never allow children to touch or squash creatures. Avoid stinging insects, and wash hands after looking. An adult leads the search.

differentiation.support: Hold the magnifying glass together and point to what you see.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count the legs on a picture of an ant.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "We are kind to small creatures."
lessons.homeConnection: Look for ants or beetles with your child and watch without touching.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name ants and beetles and look at them with a magnifying glass" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Butterflies and bees
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name a butterfly and a bee and say what they do.
successCriteria: Names a butterfly and a bee
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, their homes and babies and handle toys gently.
resources: Pictures of a butterfly and a bee
A paper butterfly on a stick
lessons.starter: Fly a paper butterfly in the air and say "Flutter, flutter. This is a butterfly."
teacherActivities: Show the butterfly and bee pictures and say the names and colours.
Move the scarf like a butterfly and like a bee.
Let each child be a butterfly or a bee and visit a flower.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children point to the flower.
Children flutter and buzz.
Child moves to the flower and back.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the butterfly and bee pictures and say the names and colours. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Butterflies and bees visit flowers." Children: Children point to the flower.
Step 3. Teacher: Move the scarf like a butterfly and like a bee. Children: Children flutter and buzz.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child be a butterfly or a bee and visit a flower. Children: Child moves to the flower and back.

practical.title: Butterflies and bees
steps: Put a flower picture on the floor.
Children fly like butterflies and bees to the flower.
practical.safety: Clear the floor so children can move safely. Do not touch real bees and stay away from hives.

differentiation.support: Fly together and say flutter or buzz.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say why bees visit flowers.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names a butterfly and a bee
lessons.conclusion: Settle like a butterfly on a flower.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for butterflies on flowers with your child and stay still to watch.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name a butterfly and a bee and say what they do" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Garden hunt
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will go on a garden hunt for small creatures and look without touching.
successCriteria: Finds a small creature or its home
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, their homes and babies and handle toys gently.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we go on a creature hunt. We have kind eyes. We look but we do not touch."
teacherActivities: Walk to the garden in a line with an adult at each end.
Search near plants, stones and leaves for small creatures.
When a creature is found, ask "What is it?"
Come back and talk about what we saw.
learnerActivities: Children walk in a line.
Children look closely with magnifiers.
Child names the creature or says small.
Child tells one thing they saw.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk to the garden in a line with an adult at each end. Children: Children walk in a line.
Step 2. Teacher: Search near plants, stones and leaves for small creatures. Children: Children look closely with magnifiers.
Step 3. Teacher: When a creature is found, ask "What is it?" Children: Child names the creature or says small.
Step 4. Teacher: Come back and talk about what we saw. Children: Child tells one thing they saw.

practical.title: Creature hunt
steps: Go to the garden in a line.
Look without touching and tell what you see.
practical.safety: Check the area for stinging insects, sharp objects and snakes before the hunt. Keep children together and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point to creatures.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count how many different creatures they saw.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What did you find?
questions.expected: An ant, a beetle or a leaf.

expectedOutcomes: Finds small creatures in the garden
lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "We were kind."
lessons.homeConnection: Look in your garden or compound for small creatures with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "go on a garden hunt for small creatures and look without touching" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Be kind to small creatures
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will say and show how to be kind to small creatures.
successCriteria: Says one way to be kind
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, their homes and babies and handle toys gently.
resources: Pictures of kind and unkind actions
lessons.starter: Hold a toy ant and say "Little ant. How can we be kind to him?"
teacherActivities: Show pictures of gentle hands and ask "Is it kind?"
Show pictures of squashing or throwing and ask "Is it kind?"
Show how to move a toy ant gently on a leaf.
Say "We look and we are gentle."
learnerActivities: Children say yes or no.
Children shake their heads and say no.
Children move the ant gently.
Children say the sentence.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of gentle hands and ask "Is it kind?" Children: Children say yes or no.
Step 2. Teacher: Show pictures of squashing or throwing and ask "Is it kind?" Children: Children shake their heads and say no.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to move a toy ant gently on a leaf. Children: Children move the ant gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We look and we are gentle." Children: Children say the sentence.

practical.title: Kind hands
steps: Give each child a toy creature and a leaf.
practical.safety: Use soft toy creatures and remind children never to squash real creatures. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Move the toy together with gentle hands.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend why we are kind to small creatures.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is it kind to squash an ant?

expectedOutcomes: Says and shows how to be kind to creatures
lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say "We are kind."
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child how to watch small creatures gently.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say and show how to be kind to small creatures" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 creatures check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names small creatures and looks gently.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, their homes and babies and handle toys gently.
lessons.starter: Sing the creature song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: pictures, magnifiers and kind hands.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "Are we kind?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children wash hands and tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: pictures, magnifiers and kind hands. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "Are we kind?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Creature stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Wash hands after each activity.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend how to look at creatures.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names small creatures; looks closely; says we do not hurt creatures.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about being kind to small creatures.
